text:
Miles Thornton: kicking off the delivery lag SLO convo for audit logs. we need something we can ship w/ the beta + something that won’t page us nonstop.

Miles Thornton: definitions first: “delivery lag” = time from `event_time` (when service emits) to “available to customer” (query API + exports). do we want to measure to `persisted_at` in the audit store, or to `exported_at` for sinks too?

Sean Gallagher: +1 on clarifying. for paging i’d rather base on core pipeline (ingest->validate->store) and have separate alerts for exporter sinks. otherwise every customer’s broken splunk endpoint wakes us up.

Rafael Mendes: agree. for product/SOC2 evidence we can say “audit events are recorded within X” (store). exports are best-effort w/ retries + DLQ, but not the SLO.

Nadia Rahman: fwiw we already emit timestamps at a few stages in the pipeline:
- `enqueued_at` (gateway)
- `persisted_at` (audit-log-pipeline)
- `export_attempted_at` / `exported_at` (exporter)
we can compute `persisted_at - event_time` fairly reliably. exporter side is trickier w/ per-sink.

Allison Grant: pls don’t use `enqueued_at` as the start time. services can be off by a bit. canonical should be `event_time` from the event envelope (schema v1) and require NTP-ish bounds.

Miles Thornton: ok propose:
SLO = “audit events persisted and queryable”
Metric = `auditlog_delivery_lag_seconds` = `persisted_at - event_time`
Measure: p99 + availability style? (e.g., “99.9% of events in 2m”)

Aisha Bello: i put up a draft grafana board with histograms + queue depth. link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/auditlog-lag/audit-log-delivery-lag (draft)
panels:
- p50/p95/p99 lag
- `auditlog_pipeline_queue_depth`
- `auditlog_events_persisted_total` vs `auditlog_events_received_total`
- exporter failures (separate row)

Sean Gallagher: what are we seeing baseline in prod right now?

Rafael Mendes: last 7d in us-east:
- p95 ~ 4-8s
- p99 ~ 20-45s
we had that exporter backlog incident (but persisted stayed fine).

Miles Thornton: nice. so SLO can be somewhat tight but should allow for deployments, regional issues. i’d go:
- SLO target: 99.9% of events persisted within 120s (2m)
- “healthy” objective: p99 < 60s most of the time

Allison Grant: 99.9% within 2m sounds ok for audit logs. also we should explicitly define “drop” vs “delay” (this came up in ENG-2489).
Drop = event accepted by ingest but never persisted (data loss)
Delay = persisted after threshold.

Nadia Rahman: +1. drop should be near-zero and should page immediately.
we have `auditlog_events_received_total` (post-validate) and `auditlog_events_persisted_total`. if persisted < received by more than ~N for 5m, that’s suspicious.

Aisha Bello: can do two alert families:
1) delivery lag (delay)
2) drop / ingestion errors (loss)
for lag i suggest warning vs critical.

Sean Gallagher: concrete thresholds pls.

Aisha Bello: proposal (per region):
- Warning: p99(lag) > 120s for 15m
- Critical: p99(lag) > 300s (5m) for 10m
- Critical drop: rate(`auditlog_persist_failures_total`) > 0 for 5m OR `received - persisted` gap increasing for 10m
also add “queue depth” symptom alert: `auditlog_pipeline_queue_depth` > 100k for 10m (tune per env)

Miles Thornton: 120s warning seems… kinda high? but i get it.
what about paging only on critical + drop, and warning is slack-only.

Rafael Mendes: yep. we should page only if customers would notice or if we risk losing evidence. lag warning goes to #eng-sre + open a linear task if it’s persistent.

PagerDuty: (configured by Aisha Bello) Proposed routing: audit-log-pipeline critical -> SRE Oncall; warnings -> #eng-sre.

Sean Gallagher: ok, and runbook should be explicit. do we have a runbook yet?

Miles Thornton: draft in confluence exists but needs these thresholds + “what to check” steps.
link: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Audit+Log+Delivery+Lag+Runbook (draft)

Rafael Mendes: adding suggested steps here so we can copy/paste:
1) check dashboard: lag panels + queue depth
2) check audit-log-pipeline deploys in last 1h (rollouts can stall consumers)
3) check consumer group lag (kafka) / queue backlog (depending on region)
4) if backlog: scale consumers + verify CPU/GPU (?) saturation; look for hot partitions
5) check validation errors spike (schema rejects) -> may indicate a bad deploy emitting invalid events
6) if persist failures: check storage (writes throttled), error logs for `persist` path, region-specific issues
7) exporter row: if only exporter failing, do NOT page pipeline (separate oncall / ticket). confirm persisted is healthy.

Allison Grant: also call out “don’t sample audit logs.” saw that question pop up last week. for lag issues we scale, we don’t reduce volume.

Nadia Rahman: one more: we should include an “event-time skew” panel. if some service starts emitting `event_time` wildly in the past/future, lag calc explodes.
maybe alert on `abs(now - event_time)` > 10m for >1% of events.

Aisha Bello: i can add that. metric we have is `auditlog_event_time_skew_seconds` (computed in pipeline) but it’s not on the board yet.

Sean Gallagher: decision check:
- SLO: 99.9% persisted within 2m (per region)
- paging: critical p99 > 5m for 10m OR any persist failures/drop suspicion
- warning: p99 > 2m for 15m (slack)
- exporter: separate alerts per sink, not part of delivery SLO
works for me.

Miles Thornton: +1

Rafael Mendes: +1

Allison Grant: +1, just add the drop definition to the runbook + the doc that Olga uses for controls.

Aisha Bello: ack. i’ll:
- update grafana board (skew panel + thresholds)
- open PR in observability-pack for alerts once we finalize numbers

Grafana Bot: Dashboard updated: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/auditlog-lag/audit-log-delivery-lag (rev 17)

Miles Thornton: action items:
- @Aisha Bello: wire alert rules + slack/pager routing
- @Rafael Mendes: update runbook w/ steps + drop vs delay
- @Nadia Rahman: confirm metric names match what we want to standardize (`auditlog_delivery_lag_seconds`, `auditlog_events_*`)
- @Sean Gallagher: sanity check paging thresholds w/ oncall load

Sean Gallagher: cool. pls also note in runbook “when to escalate to Telemetry vs Storage team”

Rafael Mendes: will do. also adding: if backlog is exporter-only, create ticket for Svetlana/Kevin, not SRE page.

Miles Thornton: thanks all. once alerts are in, we can reference them from the audit logging telemetry standards doc.
